back: The name of a particular person, place, organisation, day or month; it always starts with a capital letter.
notes: Examples: Chipo, Gweru, ZIMSEC, Monday, December.

back: A noun that names a group of people, animals or things as one unit.
notes: Team, committee, jury, herd, flock, swarm, fleet, bunch.

back: A noun that names an idea, quality, feeling or state that cannot be seen or touched.
notes: Kindness, freedom, fear, honesty, childhood, wisdom.

back: Countable nouns have plurals and take a/an (a book, two books). Uncountable nouns have no plural and no a/an (advice, furniture, information, luggage, equipment, news).
notes: Count uncountables with a unit: a piece of advice, an item of news.

front: Plurals of nouns ending in -f or -fe
back: Many change to -ves: knife → knives, leaf → leaves, wife → wives, thief → thieves, half → halves.
notes: Exceptions add -s: roofs, chiefs, cliffs, beliefs.

back: child → children, man → men, woman → women, tooth → teeth, foot → feet, mouse → mice, ox → oxen.
notes: Some stay the same: sheep, deer, fish (usually), aircraft.

back: crisis → crises, analysis → analyses, phenomenon → phenomena, criterion → criteria, cactus → cacti, medium → media.
The main noun takes the plural: mothers-in-law, passers-by, commanders-in-chief.
scissors, trousers, spectacles, pliers, clothes, police, cattle, people: they take plural verbs.
notes: The police are investigating; my trousers are torn.

back: nephew/niece, uncle/aunt, host/hostess, heir/heiress, bridegroom/bride, widower/widow, bull/cow, cock/hen.
